Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:10:1.hebrew: אני ה' אלהיכם - הוא לשון: אני אדון לכם:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:10:1.english: I am the Lord your God - It is an expression of "I am a master over you."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:12:1.hebrew: אף כאן באמצע - והיום תשע ברכות הן, ואומרה בחמישית:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:12:1.english: So too here, in the middle - And [on Rosh Hashanah] the day has nine blessings, and one recites it in the fifth [blessing].

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:13:1.hebrew: ירד רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא לפני התיבה - לפי שמצוה להתפלל במקום נמוך, קתני "ירד":
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:13:1.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka descended before the ark - Because it is a mitzvah to pray in a low place, [the baraita] teaches "descended."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:13:2.hebrew: כר' יוחנן בן נורי - הנזכר דמתניתין:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:13:2.english: Like Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri - [the one mentioned] in the Mishnah.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:13:3.hebrew: לא כך היו נוהגין ביבנה - בימי אבא, כשהיתה סנהדרין שם:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:13:3.english: They were not accustomed to act this way in Yavne - In the days of my father, when the Sanhedrin was there.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:16:1.english: One does not recite fewer than ten verses of Kingship, etc.:

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:17:1.hebrew: הנך דכתיב בהו הללוהו בתקע שופר - הנך דהללו אל בקדשו:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:17:1.english: Those regarding which it is written, "Praise Him with the blast of the shofar" - Those [verses] of "Praise God in His sanctuary" (Psalms 150:1):

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:18:1.hebrew: כנגד עשרת הדברות - דכתיב בהו נמי שופר. ולא שמעתיה, אלא ראיתיה ביסוד רבינו יצחק בן יהודה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:18:1.english: Corresponding to the Ten Commandments - For in them too, a shofar is written. I did not hear this [explanation] but I saw it in the composition of Rabbeinu Yitzchak ben Yehuda.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:18:2.english: The ten utterances by which the world was created - on Rosh Hashanah.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:19:1.hebrew: בראשית נמי מאמר הוא - ואף על גב דלא כתיב ביה "ויאמר יהי שמים", כמאן דכתיב דמי, דבאמירה נמי איברי ולא בידים, דכתיב (תהילים ל״ג:ו׳) "בדבר ה' שמים נעשו":
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:19:1.english: "In the beginning" is also an utterance - Even though "And He said, 'Let there be heaven'" is not written regarding it, it is considered as if it were written, for [the heavens] too were created by speech and not by hand, as it is written (Psalms 33:6): "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:1:1.hebrew: וקבעיה בשמיה - למנותה עם שאר תקנותיו, ולהכי תנא תשע תקנות:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:1:1.english: And his teacher established it in his name - To count it with his other ordinances; and therefore [the Tanna] taught nine ordinances.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:20:1.hebrew: היכי קתני - האי דר' יוחנן בן נורי האי "מכולם" דקאמר, אמאן קאי? אתורה נביאים וכתובים קאי, דהא מכולהו אמר, כדתנן: מתחיל בתורה ומשלים בנביא. והכי קאמר: אם אמר שלש מן התורה, ושלש מן הנביאים, ושלש מן הכתובים — מכל אחת ואחת — יצא. ולא פליג אדרבנן אלא אחדא, דאינהו אמרי עשרה, ואיהו אמר תשעה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:20:1.english: How does it teach? - This statement of Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, this "from all of them" that he says — to what does it refer? It refers to Torah, Prophets, and Writings, for he says [it] about all of them, as we learned [in the mishnah]: One begins with the Torah and concludes with the Prophets. And this is what he is saying: If one recited three from the Torah, three from the Prophets, and three from the Writings — from each and every one — he has fulfilled [his obligation]. And he does not disagree with the Rabbis except on one [verse], for they say ten, and he says nine.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:20:2.hebrew: או דלמא - האי ג' ג' אמלכיות וזכרונות ושופרות קאי: שלש למלכיות, ושלש לזכרונות, ושלש לשופרות, דהוו להו אחת מן התורה, ואחת מן הנביאים, ואחת מן הכתובים:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:20:2.english: Or perhaps - This "three, three" refers to Malchiyot, Zichronot, and Shofarot: three for Malchiyot, three for Zichronot, and three for Shofarot, so that they amount to one from the Torah, one from the Prophets, and one from the Writings:

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:22:1.hebrew: לא יפחות משבע וכו' - ואי סלקא דעתך שלש מן התורה, ושלש מן הנביאים, ושלש מן הכתובים לכל ברכה — אם כן, שבע נמי: שבע מן התורה, ושבע מן הנביאים, ושבע מן הכתובים — הוה ליה רבי יוחנן בן נורי מוסיף:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:22:1.english: He should not recite fewer than seven, etc. - And if it enters your mind that he means three from the Torah, three from the Prophets, and three from the Writings for each blessing — then if so, for the seven too it would mean seven from the Torah, seven from the Prophets, and seven from the Writings, and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri would be adding to the requirement:

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:23:1.english: One does not mention Remembrance etc.:

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:2:1.english: The order of the blessings: One recites the Patriarchs and the Mighty Deeds, etc., and the Sanctification of the Day, and sounds, etc. — For the mitzvah is [to sound] three sets of three blasts each, as taught below in this chapter (Rosh Hashanah 33b):

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:5:1.hebrew: רחמנא אמר אידכר - כדתניא בברייתא לקמן:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:5:1.english: The Merciful One said, “Mention” - As it was taught in a baraita below:

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:5:2.hebrew: לימא תשע דהואיל ואשתני - מלכיות מזכרונות, לענין תקיעה שאין תוקעין בהן, אשתנו נמי לפחות מהן:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:5:2.english: Let him say nine, since it is different - Kingship [verses] differ from Remembrances [verses] with regard to shofar-blowing, as one does not blow the shofar for them; let them also differ by having fewer [verses] than they have.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:6:1.hebrew: בני אלים - לישנא דתקיפי, כמו "ואת אילי הארץ לקח" (יחזקאל י״ז:י״ג):
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:6:1.english: Sons of the mighty - An expression of strong ones, like "and he took the mighty ones of the land" (Ezekiel 17:13).

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:6:2.hebrew: הבו לה' - הזכירו לפניו את האיתנים:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:6:2.english: Ascribe to the Lord - Mention before Him the mighty ones.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:8:1.hebrew: מפני מה לא נאמר שבתון שבות שהרי פתח בו הכתוב תחילה - והוא בא להזהיר על המלאכה, שהיא עיקר. וכך יפה לדרוש, הואיל והוא ראשון במקרא, והשביתה ראשונה לכולם:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:8:1.english: Why isn't it said that "shabbaton" [means] cessation, since the verse began with it first - For it comes to warn about [prohibited] labor, which is the main point. And it is fitting to expound in this way, since it is first in the verse, and the cessation [from work] comes first of all [the terms]:

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:9:1.hebrew: אני ה' אלהיכם - דלעני ולגר תעזוב אותם, וסמיך ליה "בחדש השביעי זכרון תרועה":
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 32a:9:1.english: I am the Lord your God - [This verse appears] at the end of the passage "for the poor and for the stranger you shall leave them," and juxtaposed to it is "In the seventh month, a remembrance of blasts."

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 32a:23:1.hebrew: מתחיל בתורה ומסיים בנביא - וא"ת, דבכל דוכתא משמע דנביאי עדיף מכתובים, כדאמר (מנילה דף לא.): כתוב בתורה, ושנוי בנביאים, ומשולש בכתובים. וה"ק: קראי דכתיבי בכתובי ברישא, והדר בנביאי? וי"ל, משום דקראי דתהלים משלי ואיוב קדמו לנביאים. ומה שאנו נוהגים להשלים בתורה — דעבדינן כרבי יוסי, כדאמרינן בגמרא: המשלים בתורה זריז ומשובח, וכן היו וותיקין עושין:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 32a:23:1.english: One begins with the Torah and concludes with the Prophets - And if you ask: In every place it implies that the Prophets are preferable to the Writings, as it says (Megillah 31a): "It is written in the Torah, repeated in the Prophets, and triplicated in the Writings." So [on this basis] it should have said: the verses written in the Writings first, and afterward those of the Prophets? And one can answer: Because the verses of Psalms, Proverbs, and Job preceded the Prophets [in time]. And as for our practice of concluding with the Torah — we act in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, as we say in the Gemara: One who concludes with the Torah is diligent and praiseworthy, and so the early pious ones (vatikin) would do.
